title: Deepest path after dropping the free-literal prefix
statement: Let $t$ be a term on $n$ variables whose literals have pairwise distinct variables, let $\rho_0$ and $\sigma$ be restrictions on $n$ variables, and let $c$ be a continuation sending each restriction to a decision tree. Let $S$ be the sub-tree built for $t$ under $\rho_0$ with continuation $c$, and let $\pi$ denote its deepest root-to-leaf path. Write $F$ for the sublist of $t$ consisting of those literals whose variable is free under $\rho_0$, and set $m = |F|$. Suppose $L$ is a list of $m$ literal–index pairs whose literal components are exactly $F$, in order, and that $P$ is a list of variable–direction pairs coinciding with the length-$|P|$ prefix of $\pi$, with $m \le |P| \le |\pi|$. Then dropping the first $m$ entries of $\pi$ leaves exactly the deepest path of $c$ evaluated at the restriction obtained from $\rho_0$ and $\sigma$ by processing the literals $L$ against the path $P$ (the updated $\rho_0$ component that this process returns).
hypotheses_covered: t is a term whose literals have pairwise distinct variables
rho_0 and sigma are restrictions on n variables
c is a continuation from restrictions to decision trees
L has length equal to the number of free literals of t under rho_0
the literals of L equal, in order, the free literals of t under rho_0

the number of free literals is at most the length of P
the length of P is at most the length of the deepest path of the sub-tree
